Subject: NorthBay — requested SLA variance and cap on service credits (initial)

Hi Stephanie,

Quick summary: NorthBay (they're on the cusp of a $1.1M ARR committed Dedicated seat) asked for a small relaxation of our standard uptime SLO in the contract. They want a 99.85% uptime target for the first 12 months (we default to 99.9%), and an explicit per-incident credit cap that is higher than our standard. They are also asking us to exclude transient latency spikes in the remedy calculation (their product team is sensitive to occasional warm-up behavior).

Attached is the redline from their legal counsel (NB_SLA_redline_v3.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan. The commercial ask is: 10% one-time onboarding credit + acceptance of the 99.85% uptime for 12 months, and a maximum single-incident credit of 5% of monthly invoice (our standard is 2.5%).

I think we can accept the onboarding credit, but the SLO and credit cap are out of policy without exec sign-off. Can you help route to Deal Desk / Aditya for an override? We need an answer by EOD Thursday to keep the signature timeline.

Thanks — I pasted a short risk note below.

Risk note: The 99.85% change materially increases the annual exposure to credits if they experience multiple incidents. Their traffic patterns are bursty (batch imports) which could increase incident frequency in month-1.

Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Aditya — forwarding Marcus's note. TL;DR: NorthBay requests 99.85% uptime for 12 months (vs our 99.9%) and a single-incident credit cap of 5% (we standard at 2.5%), plus a 10% onboarding credit. They want response by Thursday.

My read: onboarding credit is fine from a commercial standpoint; the uptime variance and larger credit cap increase financial exposure. If we accept a lower uptime target, I'd like to: 1) limit it to the first 6 months not 12, or 2) add a clause excluding scheduled maintenance and warm-up windows and tighten incident definitions.

Request: can you sign a Deal Desk variance to allow either (A) 99.85% for 6 months + 3% single-incident cap, or (B) 99.85% for 12 months but cap single incident at 3% and a total annual credit cap of 10%? If you approve, I'll get Legal to push the updated redline back to them and we can prepare the DocuSign.

Ryan / Leah — thanks for your patience. We've reviewed your requested redline and obtained executive clearance on a controlled variance. Final agreed terms (high level):

  - Uptime SLO: 99.85% for the first 12 months
  - Single-incident credit: capped at 3% of monthly invoice
  - Annual aggregate credit cap: 8% of annualized fees
  - Warm-up exclusion: first 30 minutes of an incident may be excluded where reproducible telemetry demonstrates cache/kv warm-up behavior
  - Onboarding credit: one-time 10% credit applied to first invoice
